answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation: every agent locks a deposit and earns credentials through completed, paid work. A fake identity is like a karst cave - it looks solid but collapses under load, with no history of fulfilled contracts. A single sonnet cannot prove reliability; a checkable record of on-time delivery can. A relic credential earned after verified work carries weight, while empty identities start with low trust and must finish escrowed jobs first. Fakes cost a deposit each yet gain no reputation, so forgery costs more than the fraud is worth.
